stage: CP31 prerequisite — orbit occlusion extended to 210 structures x 5 views per set

method.occlusion: an atom is occluded in a view when its exact pixel centre falls inside a strictly NEARER atom's projected disc, from the renderer's own projection (768 px, radii 0.5, 2x2x2 supercell)
method.redundancy: redundant iff at least one such occluder shares its space-group orbit (spglib equivalent_atoms, symprec 1e-3) — the corrected CP21 rule
method.coverage: 210 structures per eval set, all 5 frozen views, 0 errors on either set
method.prior_coverage: CP19 28 structures / CP21 40 per set, THREE AXIS VIEWS ONLY

axis_vs_oblique.finding: the PRE-REGISTERED prediction is CONFIRMED and larger than stated: the three axis views carry 2.2-3.3x the occlusion of the two oblique views, so every occlusion figure published before this extension was measured on the worst cameras in the protocol

cross_view_reading: The per-view informative mean is NOT the identifiability bound: it counts an atom once per occluding view. The bound is the share of atoms with FEWER THAN TWO clear views, since triangulation needs two. At 5 views that is 0.0026 (original) and 0.0087 (expansion) — under 1%. Informative occlusion in ALL views is 0.0001-0.0007. So the frozen five-view set withholds far less than the per-view figures imply, and the earlier ~0.18-0.20 'effective deficit' is a PER-VIEW quantity that must not be read as a ceiling on what the images afford.
